topics.title: Hierarchy of Quadrilaterals
topics.concept:
What is a Quadrilateral?

A quadrilateral is a polygon with 4 sides and 4 angles.

Quadrilateral Family Tree:

                        QUADRILATERAL
                      (4 sides, 4 angles)
                             │
            ┌────────────────┼────────────────┐
            │                │                │
        TRAPEZOID        PARALLELOGRAM     (Other: kite, etc.)
      (1 pair of    (2 pairs of parallel
       parallel           sides)
         sides)              │
                ┌────────────┼────────────┐
                │            │            │
            RECTANGLE     RHOMBUS       SQUARE?
            (4 right   (4 equal sides,   (special case!)
             angles)    not right angles)
                │            │
                └──────┬─────┘
                       │
                    SQUARE
            (4 right angles + 4 equal sides)

Quadrilateral Hierarchy:

ShapeProperties
Trapezoid1 pair of parallel sides
Parallelogram2 pairs of parallel sides, opposite sides equal
RectangleParallelogram + 4 right angles
RhombusParallelogram + 4 equal sides
SquareRectangle + Rhombus (4 right angles + 4 equal sides)

examples.problem: A shape has 2 pairs of parallel sides and 4 right angles. What is it?
examples.solution:
• 2 pairs of parallel sides = parallelogram
  • 4 right angles = rectangle
  • Could also be square if sides equal, but rectangle is correct
  • Answer: Rectangle

examples.problem: Draw the hierarchy from widest to narrowest: square, quadrilateral, rectangle, parallelogram
examples.solution:
• Widest: Quadrilateral
  • Then: Parallelogram
  • Then: Rectangle
  • Narrowest: Square
  • Answer: Quadrilateral → Parallelogram → Rectangle → Square

examples.problem: A trapezoid has how many pairs of parallel sides?
examples.solution:
• Definition of trapezoid: exactly 1 pair of parallel sides
  • Answer: 1 pair

topics.title: Classifying Triangles by Sides
topics.concept:
What is a Triangle?

A triangle is a polygon with 3 sides and 3 angles. Sum of angles = 180°.

Classification by Sides:

TypeDescriptionExample
EquilateralAll 3 sides EQUAL3 cm, 3 cm, 3 cm
Isosceles2 sides EQUAL5 cm, 5 cm, 3 cm
ScaleneNO sides equal4 cm, 5 cm, 6 cm

Classification by Angles:

TypeDescriptionExample
AcuteAll angles < 90°60°, 60°, 60°
RightOne angle = 90°30°, 60°, 90°
ObtuseOne angle > 90°30°, 30°, 120°

examples.problem: A triangle has sides 6 cm, 6 cm, and 8 cm. How would you classify it by sides?
examples.solution:
• Two sides equal (6 and 6)
  • Therefore isosceles triangle
  • Answer: Isosceles

examples.problem: A triangle has angles 35°, 55°, and 90°. Classify by angles.
examples.solution:
• One angle = 90° (right angle)
  • Therefore right triangle
  • Answer: Right triangle

examples.problem: A triangle has sides 5 cm, 7 cm, 9 cm and angles 35°, 55°, 90°. Give both classifications.
examples.solution:
• Sides: all different → scalene
  • Angles: one 90° → right
  • Answer: Right scalene triangle

examples.problem: Can a triangle be both equilateral and right?
examples.solution:
• Equilateral = all angles 60°
  • Right triangle = one angle 90°
  • 60° ≠ 90°, so impossible
  • Answer: No

recap: Equilateral = all sides equal + all angles 60°
Isosceles = 2 sides equal + 2 base angles equal
Scalene = no sides equal + all angles different
Every triangle has TWO classifications (by sides AND by angles)
